dedupe_keys.name: open government geospatial data on buildings global benchmark of 140 releases from 28 countries

description: A 2021 study by Filip Biljecki, Lawrence Chew, Nikola Milojevic-Dupont and Felix Creutzig that surveys the 2D building data released by governments for free access, from single cities to whole countries. The authors identified and benchmarked more than 140 releases from 28 countries, holding over 100 million buildings, on five dimensions: accessibility, richness of attributes, data quality, harmonisation, and relationships with other actors. They find much government building data is valuable for spatial analysis but with large disparities: not all instances are of high quality, harmonised or rich in descriptive attributes. The study also compares authoritative data with OpenStreetMap and finds a mutually beneficial, complementary relationship, with supplementary information comparing coverage in the European Union. The paper counts only data that can be freely used, modified and shared, excluding data offered for a charge or for viewing only. Format and access: an open PDF on arXiv; whether the list of releases is published as a separate file was not found. Licence: the arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence for the paper; no open reuse licence. Caveats: a 2021 snapshot. Useful as a guide to which national and city building datasets exist for exposure, energy and adaptation planning; related records are not yet linked.
